verifications.claim: A solemn assembly in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is used for sustaining a new Church President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "sustaining of a new prophet and First Presidency" (R1); "sustaining of a new Church president" (R2); "sustaining a new President of the Church" (R3); "sustaining of new Church presidents" (R5); "sustain President Dallin H. Oaks as prophet" (R7); "sustaining a new church president" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state solemn assemblies are used for sustaining a new Church President.

verifications.claim: A solemn assembly in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is used for dedicating temples.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "dedications of temples" (R1); "dedication of a temple" (R2); "dedication of temples" (R3); "dedication of a temple" (R5); "dedication of the Kirtland Temple" (R6); "dedications of temples" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly list temple dedications as a purpose of solemn assemblies.

verifications.claim: A solemn assembly in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is used for special instruction.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "instruction of priesthood leaders" (R2); "special instruction to priesthood leaders" (R3); "provide instruction to church leaders" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm use for special instruction to priesthood or church leaders.

verifications.claim: Solemn assemblies are primarily used to sustain a newly called President of the Church.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Sources list sustaining new President as one key purpose among others like temple dedications and instruction (e.g., "three purposes: dedication of temples, special instruction..., sustaining a new President" (R3))
verifications.reasoning: Sources support sustaining new President as a major use but list it alongside others without stating it is 'primarily' used for that.

verifications.claim: In solemn assemblies, members are asked to stand and sustain the First Presidency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "stand when requested and express your choice to sustain" (R1); "stand and manifest by the uplifted right hand... First Presidency" (R2); "priesthood quorums... stand... First Presidency" (R3); "sustain... members of the First Presidency" (R7); "sustain the new president, along with his counselors" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct descriptions of standing to sustain First Presidency in solemn assemblies.

verifications.claim: In solemn assemblies, members are asked to stand and sustain the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Quorum of the Twelve Apostles" (R2); "The other leaders of the Church are similarly sustained" after President (R3); "Quorum of the Twelve Apostles" (R7); "Quorum of the Twelve Apostles" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly include standing to sustain Quorum of the Twelve.

verifications.claim: In solemn assemblies, members are asked to stand and sustain other senior leaders.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "General Authority Seventies... Presiding Bishopric; Area Seventies" (R2); "The other leaders of the Church are similarly sustained" (R3); "other senior leaders" (R7); "Quorums of Seventy and Presiding Bishopric" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe sustaining various senior leaders beyond First Presidency and Twelve.

verifications.claim: Sustaining in solemn assemblies is typically organized by quorums.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "sustaining vote... by quorums and groups" (R1); "priesthood quorums, commencing with the First Presidency" (R2, R3); "groups of church members are asked to stand in succession" including quorums (R8); "stand in quorums, or groups" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm organization by quorums and groups standing in sequence.

verifications.claim: A solemn assembly was held during the Saturday morning session of the April 2026 general conference to sustain the new First Presidency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "solemn assembly during the Saturday morning session of the April 2026 general conference... sustain our new prophet... and his two counselors" (R1); "solemn assembly... during the Saturday morning session of April 2026... sustain a new Church president and First Presidency" (R2); "Saturday morning session" (R4); "Saturday morning session of the April 2026... sustained... First Presidency" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the exact event, session, and purpose.

verifications.claim: A solemn assembly was held in April 2020 for the 200th anniversary of the First Vision.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 5, 2020... commemorated the 200th anniversary of Joseph Smith’s First Vision" (R1); "April 2020 general conference to commemorate the 200th anniversary of the First Vision" (R4); "April 5, 2020, to commemorate the 200th anniversary of Joseph Smith's... First Vision" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm the April 2020 solemn assembly for the First Vision anniversary.

verifications.claim: The April 2020 solemn assembly included the Hosanna Shout.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "included a Hosanna Shout" (R1); "included the Hosanna Shout" (R4); "included a hosanna shout" (R8)

verifications.claim: The phrase of the Hosanna Shout comes from the Hebrew Bible.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute 'solemn assembly' to Hebrew Bible but Hosanna Shout to New Testament roots (R2); no source links Hosanna Shout phrase directly to Hebrew Bible.

verifications.claim: The phrase represents special gatherings during the Passover and the Feast of Tabernacles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "phrase “solemn assembly”... sacred gatherings that happened during Passover and the Feast of Tabernacles" (R1); "important gatherings... during Passover and the Feast of the Tabernacles" (R6); "feast day at the end of Passover and... Feast of Tabernacles" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state 'solemn assembly' phrase describes such biblical gatherings.

verifications.claim: The first modern solemn assembly was held at the Kirtland Temple dedication in 1836.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Solemn assembly at Kirtland Temple dedication On March 27, 1836" (R2); "first solemn assembly was held in the Kirtland Temple on 27 March 1836" (R3); "dedication of the Kirtland Temple on March 27, 1836" (R5); "first... in modern times... Kirtland Temple... 1836" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Kirtland Temple dedication in 1836 as the first modern solemn assembly.

verifications.claim: The practice of raising hands and standing to sustain the prophet began with President John Taylor.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "pattern... established by the Prophet Joseph Smith" at Kirtland (R2, R3); "first solemn assembly to sustain a new prophet... John Taylor" but pattern from Kirtland where Joseph was sustained as prophet (R1, R8); "began with President Taylor following the pattern at the Kirtland Temple" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources state the practice/pattern originated at Kirtland Temple (Joseph Smith sustained as prophet), not beginning with Taylor.

verifications.claim: President John Taylor followed a pattern set at the Kirtland Temple dedication.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "pattern, which was established by the Prophet Joseph Smith" at Kirtland (R2, R3); "following the pattern at the Kirtland Temple dedication" (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Taylor followed the Kirtland precedent/pattern.

verifications.claim: In recent assemblies like April 2018, the Melchizedek Priesthood, Relief Society, Aaronic Priesthood, Young Women, and the entire congregation stand in sequence to provide their sustaining vote.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "high priests and elders [Melchizedek]; members of the Relief Society; those holding only the Aaronic Priesthood; young women; and the entire Church membership" in April 2018 (R2); similar sequence in 2018 (R8)
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly describes the exact sequence for April 2018 solemn assembly.

verifications.claim: Some solemn assemblies include the Hosanna Shout.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In some solemn assemblies... Hosanna Shout" (R1); "Some solemn assemblies include the Hosanna Shout" (R2); "Some solemn assemblies... include the Hosanna Shout" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state some include it.

verifications.claim: The Hosanna Shout is not always part of the procedure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "not... at every solemn assembly... only... when specified... no Hosanna Shout in... 2026" (R1); "will not include the Hosanna Shout" (R2, R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it is not always included, with specific examples.
